problem: Generative visual navigation planners (NoMaD diffusion, FlowNav flow matching) start from unstructured Gaussian noise, so they need many refinement steps and produce unsafe, unimodal or overconfident plans under visual ambiguity. Learned priors like NaviBridger need an extra training stage and are unimodal.
motivation: Real-time robot navigation needs trajectories that are smooth, safe, multimodal (e.g. left vs right at a junction) and fast to generate. Replacing the noise prior with a geometry-aware prior built from the visual input should shorten refinement and preserve alternative routes.
key_idea: Learn a dense success-probability field from temporally smoothed V-JEPA2 features, extract diverse low-energy corridor trajectories from it as a multimodal mixture prior, and refine them with a regularized conditional flow matching (smoothness + safety barrier) in few steps.
insight: The structured prior is the main source of gain: in the ablation on Stanford 2D-3D-S, Gaussian prior gives SR 72.5, single-peak prior 85.3, full multimodal prior 94.8. The learned field also beats a DepthAnything depth field (SR 79.5) and direct waypoint regression (74.2), and removing DIFP drops SR to 79.8. The smoothness and safety regularizers are complementary (CFM 84.9 SR with 2.1% collisions; both terms give 94.8 SR with 0.6%), and StepNav converges within about 5 steps whereas FlowNav and NaviBridger need more than 10.
method: DIFP feature refinement: V-JEPA2 encodes the image history and goal image; features are projected onto a temporally smooth, motion-context-aligned solution in closed form, Z~=(2I+L^T L)^-1 (Z+z_c 1^T).
Success probability field: a lightweight conv decoder predicts a field F in [0,1] over space, trained against binary expert-demonstration labels with a gradient plus biharmonic smoothness penalty.
Energy landscape and K-shortest paths: E(tau)=∫-log(F+δ)||τ'|| dt; the domain is discretized into a graph and K-shortest-path search extracts low-energy candidate trajectories.

Multimodal mixture prior: a diverse subset is chosen by greedy max-min Hausdorff selection and weighted by softmax of a score (success probability, length, curvature); the initial trajectory is sampled from this mixture.
Reg-CFM: conditional flow matching from the prior sample with the loss L_FM + ρ·L_smooth (finite-difference jerk) + κ·L_safe (log-barrier with d ∝ 1-F), conditioned on z_c.
Few-step inference: Euler integration with N steps (about 5) starting from the structured prior, giving 8.5 Hz on a Jetson AGX Orin.

setting.backbone: V-JEPA2 encoder + conv success-field head + conditional flow-matching network (Reg-CFM); trained on the authors' splits
setting.training_data: NoMaD-style aggregate of RECON, SCAND, GoStanford, SACSoN (over 1,450 scenes); no extra synthetic or web data mentioned
setting.observation: monocular forward-facing RGB image history + goal image
setting.action_space: predicted trajectories (waypoint sequences), refined by flow matching
setting.simulator: Stanford 2D-3D-S (indoor) and Gazebo citysim (outdoor); real Clearpath Jackal
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert-demonstration labels used only for training the field)

numbers_note: The paper does not report standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmarks. It uses custom indoor (Stanford 2D-3D-S) and outdoor (Citysim) tasks with no official splits, so the split label 'test' is a placeholder. The refinement-step scaling results are in a figure only, with no exact numbers. Table 1 reports mean ± std, which is omitted here.
results: StepNav beats ViNT, NoMaD, NaviBridger and FlowNav on both domains. On indoor Basic it reaches SR 95 vs NaviBridger's 92, and on outdoor Basic 57 vs NaviBridger's 44. It also has the lowest MS in every setting and the lowest or tied-lowest collision rate. It runs at 8.5 Hz vs FlowNav's 6.9 Hz on a Jetson AGX Orin and converges within about 5 steps.
limitations: Evaluated on custom sim benchmarks with retrained baselines and only qualitative real-robot demos; no standard navigation benchmarks or quantitative real-world numbers.
Relies on expert-demonstration labels for the field, and dynamic environments are not modeled (planned future work); a depth field gave slightly lower collisions, suggesting depth cues are missing.
Outdoor Basic SR is still low (57%), and FlowNav has higher SPL indoors (0.81 vs 0.80).
